mainTopic: How the קרבן עולה ויורד and the inner שעיר of יום כיפור both deal with טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, and exactly which cases the שעיר covers.
overview: The גמרא finishes a גזירה שוה proving that the קרבן עולה ויורד is brought for טומאת מקדש. It then asks why the word "בָּהּ" is needed. It answers that "בָּהּ" includes someone made impure by נבלת עוף טהור, because a מיעוט אחר מיעוט comes to include. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's case of awareness at the beginning but not at the end, where the inner שעיר of יום כיפור holds off the punishment. A ברייתא shows that this שעיר does not atone for עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות or שפיכות דמים, even though the תורה calls them 'impure'. It atones only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. רבי יהודה learns this by comparison to another place, and רבי שמעון learns it from the same פסוק. The ברייתא then limits the שעיר to sins that cannot be fixed by a personal קרבן. In the case of awareness only at the start, the שעיר just holds off the punishment. Finally, the גמרא asks what case of עבודה זרה could have been suggested at all. It answers: on purpose without a warning, or by mistake without ever finding out.

steps.title: Finishing the comparison: the offering is for impurity of the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes a גזירה שוה from the פסוק about the פרה אדומה, proving that the קרבן עולה ויורד is for טומאת מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there (about the פרה אדומה) it says: "He shall be impure; his impurity is still upon him." Just as there it is talking about making the מקדש impure, so too here it is talking about making the מקדש impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a word-comparison between two פסוקים. It concludes that the קרבן in our פסוק is for someone who entered the מקדש or ate קדשים while impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same wording about impurity appears in both places. In the פרה אדומה section the פסוק clearly talks about defiling the מקדש. So the גמרא carries that meaning over to our פסוק: the קרבן עולה ויורד is about טומאת מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in the other פסוק)
Just as there... so too here (the comparison formula)
Impurity connected to the מקדש: entering it or eating קדשים while impure
A comparison learned from matching words in two פסוקים

phrases.english: And it is written there:
"He shall be impure; his impurity is still upon him";
just as there it is impurity of the Temple,
so too here it is impurity of the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַלָּן טוּמְאַת מִקְדָּשׁ, אַף כָּאן טוּמְאַת מִקְדָּשׁ
steps.raayaObject: That the קרבן עולה ויורד is brought only for טומאת מקדש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה with במדבר 19:13, where the impurity clearly relates to the מקדש

steps.title: Then why do we need the word "through which"?
steps.stepSummary: If the קרבן is only for טומאת מקדש, the word "בָּהּ" seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, why do I need the word "בָּהּ"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: now that we know the קרבן is only for the מקדש, the word "בָּהּ" seems to have no job left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, "בָּהּ" was used to teach that eating תרומה while impure does not require this קרבן. But the גזירה שוה already limits the קרבן to the מקדש, so תרומה is excluded anyway. That makes "בָּהּ" look extra.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so
Why do I need it?
"Through which" (ויקרא 5:3)

phrases.english: But then why do I need "through which"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:3. Earlier the גמרא used this word to leave out eating תרומה while impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 1 to make the word "בָּהּ" look extra
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the גזירה שוה limits the קרבן to טומאת מקדש, excluding תרומה through "בָּהּ" is unnecessary.

steps.title: It includes the carcass of a kosher bird
steps.stepSummary: "בָּהּ" comes to include a person who became impure from נבלת עוף טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include נבלת עוף טהור, the carcass of a kosher bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that "בָּהּ" has a new job: to include someone made impure by נבלת עוף טהור who then entered the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבלת עוף טהור is unusual because it makes a person impure only by eating it, not by touching it. Without a special word, we might think entering the מקדש with this impurity is not included. "בָּהּ" teaches that it is included.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (add more cases)
The carcass of a kosher bird that was not properly slaughtered

phrases.english: To include the carcass of a kosher bird.
phrases.notes: This impurity comes only from eating the bird, not from touching it, which is why it needs a special word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2 by giving "בָּהּ" a new job
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the word to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "בָּהּ" is extra once תרומה is already excluded
steps.terutzMaskana: "בָּהּ" includes impurity from נבלת עוף טהור

steps.title: But "through which" is a limiting word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: "בָּהּ" was called a restriction, so how can it include more cases?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you said "בָּהּ" is a restriction!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer: "בָּהּ" was treated as a limiting word, so it should not be able to add a case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word that limits usually takes cases away. The answer in step 3 uses the same word to add a case. That looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: But you said (pointing to an earlier claim)
A restriction, a word that limits

phrases.english: But you said "through which" is a restriction!

steps.kashyaTarget: Using "בָּהּ" to include נבלת עוף טהור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A restricting word cannot be used to include more cases.

steps.title: Two restrictions in a row include more
steps.stepSummary: Because "בָּהּ" restricts right after "או כי יגע" also restricts, it is a מיעוט אחר מיעוט, which comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: Precisely because it is a restriction, it includes. It is written "Or if he touches": an impurity that comes through touching, yes; one that does not come through touching, no. And it is written "בָּהּ", another restriction. So it is a restriction after a restriction, and a restriction after a restriction only comes to include.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that "בָּהּ" includes precisely because it is a restriction coming after another restriction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "או כי יגע" already limits the law to impurities that come by touching, which would leave out נבלת עוף טהור. "בָּהּ" adds a second limit. By the rule of מיעוט אחר מיעוט, two limits in a row cancel out and widen the law, so נבלת עוף טהור is included.

keyTerms.meaning: It is extra (and so it teaches something)
Touching
A restriction after a restriction
Only comes to include

steps.whatToRemember: "בָּהּ" includes נבלת עוף טהור because it is a second restriction after "או כי יגע", and מיעוט אחר מיעוט comes to include.
steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards, but in this rule two limiting words together widen the law instead of narrowing it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of מיעוט אחר מיעוט is a general tool for reading פסוקים that appears in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: Because it is a restriction, it is extra to include;
It is written: "Or if he touches" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:3, the start of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: something that comes through touching, yes,
something that does not come through touching, no;
and it is written "through which" — a restriction;
this is a restriction after a restriction,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת.
phrases.english: and a restriction after a restriction only comes to include.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by showing why the restricting word ends up including
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies a general reading rule (מיעוט אחר מיעוט)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A restricting word cannot include a case
steps.terutzMaskana: A second restriction after "או כי יגע" makes a מיעוט אחר מיעוט, which includes נבלת עוף טהור

steps.title: Back to the משנה: awareness at the start but not at the end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה: a person knew at the beginning but has no awareness at the end, and the inner שעיר of יום כיפור handles it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: where there was awareness at the beginning but no awareness at the end, the goat whose service is done inside, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its next clause, about the שעיר whose blood is brought inside. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1-5 dealt with the קרבן עולה ויורד for טומאת מקדש. Now the גמרא moves to a new case: the person forgot in the middle and never found out. The משנה says the inner שעיר of יום כיפור deals with this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness at the beginning: the person knew about the טומאה before he forgot
Awareness at the end: finding out afterward that he sinned
The יום כיפור goat whose blood is brought inside, into the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: Where there was awareness at the beginning
but there was no awareness at the end
the goat performed inside, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה line: this goat and יום כיפור hold off his punishment until he finds out.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּתְּחִלָּה וְאֵין בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the קרבן עולה ויורד and opens a new clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of awareness at the start but not at the end, the inner שעיר of יום כיפור is what deals with the sin.

steps.title: A ברייתא suggests the goat atones for three sins called impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes the פסוק about the inner שעיר and first suggests it could cover עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And he shall atone upon the holy place from the impurities of the children of Israel.' I could use this to include three impurities: עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, and שפיכות דמים.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings the פסוק about the inner שעיר and offers a first idea: 'impurities' might include three severe sins. This idea is set up so it can be checked and rejected in the coming steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the שעיר atones for 'טומאות'. The תורה uses the word טומאה for more than physical impurity, so one might think the שעיר covers any sin called 'impure'. This is only the starting suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall atone upon the holy place: the פסוק about the inner שעיר
Idol worship
Forbidden relations
Bloodshed, murder

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And he shall atone upon the holy place
from the impurities of the children of Israel, etc."
I have, in this matter,
grounds to include three impurities:
the impurity of idol worship,
and the impurity of forbidden relations,
and the impurity of bloodshed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְכִפֶּר עַל הַקֹּדֶשׁ מִטֻּמְאֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to explain what the שעיר from the משנה atones for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first suggestion is that the inner שעיר might atone for עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, and שפיכות דמים, since all three are called טומאה.

steps.title: Each of the three sins is called impurity in a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows that the תורה calls each of the three sins 'טומאה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: About עבודה זרה it says: 'in order to make My Sanctuary impure.' About גילוי עריות it says: 'Keep My charge, not to do any of the abominable customs, and do not become impure through them.' About שפיכות דמים it says: 'Do not make the land impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא supports the suggestion from Step 7 by showing a פסוק for each sin where the תורה uses the word 'impure'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why someone would think the שעיר covers these sins: the תורה really does call them טומאה. Each sin gets its own פסוק using a form of the word טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: In order to make My Sanctuary impure: said about idol worship
And do not become impure through them: said about forbidden relations
Do not make the land impure: said about bloodshed

phrases.english: About idol worship it says:
"in order to make My Sanctuary impure";
about forbidden relations it says:
"And you shall keep My charge
not to do any of the abominable customs, etc.
and do not become impure through them";
about bloodshed it says:
"and you shall not make the land impure."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the suggestion of Step 7 by showing that all three sins are called טומאה.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים count as 'טומאות'.

steps.title: The word 'from the impurities' means not all impurities
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the idea that the שעיר atones for those three sins, because the פסוק says 'from' the impurities, meaning only some of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think the goat atones for these three impurities. The verse teaches: 'from the impurities of the children of Israel', and not all impurities.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the suggestion from Steps 7-8. The פסוק's wording shows the שעיר does not cover every kind of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say 'the impurities'. It says 'מטמאת', from the impurities, and the extra letter מ means 'some of'. So the שעיר atones for only one kind of טומאה, and the three severe sins are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think: introduces an idea that is about to be rejected
The verse teaches: introduces the פסוק that settles the question
Atones

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying the תורה doesn't call those sins 'impure'. It does (Step 8). The point is only that this שעיר doesn't atone for them.

phrases.english: One might think that for these three impurities
the goat would atone?
The verse teaches:
"From the impurities of the children of Israel"
phrases.notes: The little letter מ, 'from', is the key: it means 'some of' the impurities.

phrases.english: and not all impurities.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל עַל שָׁלֹשׁ טְומָאוֹת הַלָּלוּ יְהֵא שָׂעִיר מְכַפֵּר? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the inner שעיר atones for עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק says 'מטמאת', from the impurities, which limits it to some impurities rather than all.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the goat atones for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה works out which impurity is meant: the one the תורה singles out elsewhere, טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do we find that the verse set apart from all impurities? You must say it is the impurity of the Temple and its holy foods. So too here, it is the impurity of the Temple and its holy foods. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know it is only some impurity, the ברייתא identifies which one. רבי יהודה says it is טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere the תורה singles out one kind of טומאה for special atonement: entering the מקדש or eating קדשים while impure, which needs a קרבן עולה ויורד. רבי יהודה compares the two: the impurity singled out there is the same one singled out here. In the next step רבי שמעון reaches the same conclusion from a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: What do we find: introduces a comparison to another place in the תורה
Entering the מקדש or eating holy food while impure
So too here: applies the comparison to our case

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the inner שעיר of יום כיפור atones only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, not for עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות or שפיכות דמים, even though the תורה calls those 'impure'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines exactly what the יום כיפור שעיר atones for. It ties it to the same sin as the קרבן עולה ויורד discussed earlier.

phrases.english: What do we find that the verse set apart
from among all impurities?
You must say: the impurity of the Temple and its holy foods;
so too here,
it is for the impurity of the Temple and its holy foods.
These are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה מָצִינוּ שֶׁחִלֵּק הַכָּתוּב מִכְּלַל כׇּל טוּמְאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 9 shows the פסוק means only some impurity, this step identifies which one.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה: the inner שעיר atones only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, learned by comparison to where the תורה singles out this impurity elsewhere.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the verse itself tells us it is about holy things
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says we do not need another פסוק. The words 'וכפר על הקדש מטמאת' already mean impurities connected to holy things.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: It is decided from its own place. The verse says 'And he shall atone for the holy place from the impurities.' This means impurities of holy things.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון reaches the same answer as רבי יהודה, that the שעיר is about טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. He gets there from a different source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה had to look at another place where the תורה singles out one kind of טומאה. רבי שמעון says the answer is in the same פסוק: the word 'הקדש' right next to 'מטמאת' tells us which impurities are meant, the ones that touch holy things.

keyTerms.meaning: It is decided from its own place (the same פסוק)
The holy place; holy things
Impurities

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
From its own place it is decided;
phrases.notes: He means we don't need to look at a different פסוק. The answer is right here.

phrases.english: for it says:
"And he shall atone for the holy place from the impurities" –
from impurities of holy things.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מִמְּקוֹמוֹ הוּא מוּכְרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the same conclusion רבי יהודה reached in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inner שעיר deals with impurities of the מקדש and its holy things, learned straight from the words 'על הקדש מטמאת'.

steps.title: Maybe the goat covers every case of defiling holy things?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the שעיר atones for every kind of טומאת מקדש, even when the person knew about it the whole time.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think this goat atones for every impurity involving holy things.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the topic is טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, the ברייתא suggests a broad reading so it can narrow it in the next line. This is a setup for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading 'all impurities of holy things' could include cases where the person knew at the start and at the end. Those cases are already handled by a personal קרבן. The question asks whether the שעיר covers them too.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (introduces an idea that will be limited)
Atones

phrases.english: One might think that for every impurity involving holy things
this goat should atone?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the topic from steps 10–11 and asks whether it is unlimited.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the שעיר cover every case of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, even ones a personal קרבן can fix?

steps.title: Only sins that cannot be fixed by a personal offering, like intentional sins
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts 'sins' next to 'rebellions' (פשעים). Rebellions cannot be atoned for by a קרבן, so the sins meant here are also ones that cannot be.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And from their rebellions, for all their sins.' The sins are like the rebellions. Rebellions are not the kind of thing you bring a קרבן for. So too, the sins meant here are ones you cannot bring a קרבן for.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 12. The שעיר does not cover every case, only cases that cannot be brought as a personal קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A personal חטאת is only for mistakes, never for deliberate sins (פשעים). Because the פסוק groups 'חטאים' with 'פשעים', the חטאים must also be ones with no קרבן option. So if the person knew at the beginning and at the end, he brings his own קרבן עולה ויורד, and the שעיר is not needed for him.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces the source)
Rebellious, deliberate sins
Similar to; like
The kind of sin that can be atoned for by a personal קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: 'חטאים' here does not mean every sin. It means only the sins that are like פשעים in one way: no personal קרבן can be brought for them.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And from their rebellions, for all their sins" –
sins that are like rebellions;
just as rebellions are not subject to an offering,
so too, sins that are not subject to an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by limiting the שעיר to cases with no personal קרבן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שעיר covers only sins that, like פשעים, cannot be atoned for by a personal קרבן.

steps.title: Where do we learn the goat only holds off punishment for 'knew at first, not at the end'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source that, when a person knew at the beginning but not at the end, the שעיר only suspends (תולה) the punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that in a case where the person knew at the beginning but did not know at the end, this goat holds off the punishment?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now asks about the case from the משנה that was quoted in step 6. It wants a source for the rule that the שעיר only holds things off here. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the person has no awareness yet, so he cannot bring a קרבן now. But he might find out later and then bring one. So the question is why the שעיר only suspends the punishment here instead of fully atoning.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?
Awareness at the beginning
Awareness at the end
Suspends; holds off the punishment for now

phrases.english: And from where do we know, for a case where there was awareness at the beginning
but there was no awareness at the end,
that this goat holds off the punishment?
phrases.notes: תולה means it doesn't fully wipe the sin away. It protects him until he finds out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 13 defined which sins the שעיר covers, this asks what exactly it does in the משנה's case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the שעיר is only תולה when there was awareness at the start but not at the end.

steps.title: 'For all their sins' includes people who may later owe a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: The word 'חטאתם' hints at people who will owe a חטאת. Since this person may later bring a קרבן, the שעיר only holds off the punishment until then.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'for all their sins.' People who are obligated in sin-offerings are included.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 14 from the words 'לכל חטאתם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חטאתם' can be read as 'their חטאות', sin-offerings. So the פסוק is talking about people who are on track to bring a חטאת once they find out. Because their real atonement will come later through that קרבן, the שעיר only protects them for now.

keyTerms.meaning: People obligated to bring sin-offerings
Included in the meaning

steps.whatToRemember: The inner שעיר: (1) is about טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, (2) only for cases with no personal קרבן option, and (3) when the person knew at the start but not at the end, it only holds off the punishment until he finds out and brings his קרבן.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "for all their sins" –
those obligated in sin-offerings are included.
phrases.notes: The word חטאתם can also mean 'their sin-offerings', so it hints at people who will owe one later.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לכל חטאתם' points to people who will owe a חטאת, so for them the שעיר is only תולה.

steps.title: The גמרא goes back and quotes the first line about the three severe sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins reviewing the ברייתא. It quotes the opening suggestion that the שעיר might cover עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: In this matter I could include three impurities: the impurity of עבודה זרה, the impurity of גילוי עריות, and the impurity of שפיכות דמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finished, and the גמרא now goes back to look closely at its details. This line just quotes the ברייתא's first idea (from step 7) to set up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is ruled here. The גמרא repeats the line so it can examine it next. In the next step it asks what case of עבודה זרה the שעיר could even cover.

keyTerms.meaning: To include
Idol worship
Forbidden relations
Bloodshed; murder

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion. The גמרא is only quoting the ברייתא from step 7 again so it can ask about it.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is the ברייתא itself, which the גמרא is now quoting back.

phrases.english: In this matter I could include
three impurities –
the impurity of idol worship,
and the impurity of forbidden relations,
and the impurity of bloodshed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: יֵשׁ לִי בְּעִנְיָן זֶה לְהָבִיא שָׁלֹשׁ טוּמְאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the ברייתא, the גמרא goes back to step 7's line to examine it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A quotation of the ברייתא's opening suggestion, setting up the גמרא's review.

steps.title: Which case of idol worship could the שעיר possibly cover?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא's suggestion about עבודה זרה could work. On purpose, the sinner gets the death penalty. By mistake, he brings his own חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This עבודה זרה, what case is it? If he did it on purpose, he deserves death! If he did it by mistake, he brings his own קרבן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's opening suggestion that the שעיר might atone for עבודה זרה. It asks what case that could even be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every case of עבודה זרה seems to be already handled. On purpose (מזיד), the punishment is death, and no קרבן atones for that. By mistake (שוגג), he brings his own חטאת, so he does not need the שעיר. Either way, it seems the ברייתא had no reason to even suggest the שעיר.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
On purpose
By mistake, without knowing it was forbidden
Someone who deserves the death penalty
Someone who must bring a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not challenging the final halacha. It is only asking how the ברייתא's first suggestion, which the ברייתא itself rejected, could even have been considered.

phrases.english: This idol worship, what are the circumstances?
If on purpose, he is subject to death!
If by mistake, he is liable to bring an offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case behind the ברייתא's opening suggestion quoted in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's suggestion that the שעיר might atone for עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: on purpose, the punishment is death, which no קרבן fixes. By mistake, he brings his own חטאת. So the שעיר has nothing left to cover.

steps.title: On purpose but no warning, or by mistake but never found out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with two in-between cases. He sinned on purpose but was never warned, so there is no death penalty. Or he sinned by mistake but never found out, so he cannot bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: On purpose, but they did not warn him. By mistake, but he never found out about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with two cases where neither death nor a personal קרבן applies. In these cases it made sense to think the שעיר might atone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית דין only gives the death penalty if witnesses warned the sinner first (התראה), so with no warning there is no execution. A חטאת is only brought once the person finds out he sinned, so if he never found out, he never brought one. These leftover cases are what the ברייתא had in mind, before it rejected the idea from the word 'מטמאת' in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: They warned him (gave התראה) before the sin
A warning from witnesses, needed before a בית דין can punish
He found out, he became aware

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ברייתא's suggestion was not silly. There really are cases of עבודה זרה with no other כפרה, so a פסוק was needed to rule them out.

phrases.english: On purpose, but they did not warn him,
By mistake, but he never became aware of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 17 by defining in-between cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: finding situations that fall outside both sides of the dilemma.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed every case of עבודה זרה was already covered by death or by a personal חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: On purpose with no warning, or by mistake with no awareness. Neither punishment applies, so it made sense to suggest the שעיר.
